title: Clean-to-dirty flow and equipment segregation
audience: Cleaners and cleaning supervisors who move between rooms and areas in residential aged care, clinics, dental practices and NDIS settings in any Australian state or territory.
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: NHMRC, Australian Guidelines for the Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare (2019), CD34 (no page date shown; document dated 2019); NDIS Practice Standards and Quality Indicators, Version 4 (November 2021), Core Module (cover date November 2021; no page date shown). Only part of these sources has been confirmed.
learningOutcomes: Plan a clean-to-dirty route through a care or clinical area that follows the facility's direction of travel.
Allocate and separate cloths, equipment and products between clean and used zones.
Recognise a cross-contamination event and state the containment and reporting step.
Record the route, the segregation used and any breach.

instruction.heading: Why the direction of travel matters
instruction.body: In a care or clinical setting, the most common way contamination spreads from one area to another is by the cleaner. A cloth used in a bathroom, a trolley wheel that rolls through a soiled corridor, or a glove that touched a bin and then a clean handle can carry an organism to the next place. The NHMRC Australian Guidelines for the Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare (document dated 2019) treat environmental controls, including cleaning and spill management, as part of preventing transmission from the environment to patients. A clean-to-dirty flow is one way the facility applies that control: work moves from the least contaminated areas toward the most contaminated, and used items move out without crossing back through clean areas.

instruction.heading: Planning the route through the area
instruction.body: Before starting, decide the route with your supervisor or the schedule. Identify the clean store, the least exposed rooms, the more exposed rooms, the holding area for used items, and the route between them. The facility may set a specific order, such as clean common areas first, then resident rooms in a set sequence, and then bathrooms and the holding area last. Follow it. If the route is blocked or the sequence cannot be followed, stop and tell the supervisor before you change it, rather than making a shortcut that crosses a contaminated area.

instruction.heading: Allocating cloths, equipment and products
instruction.body: Use separate cloths, equipment and product containers for clean and used zones, as the facility procedure directs. Many facilities use colour coding for cloths and buckets to show the zone. Keep each colour for its zone, and do not use a cloth from the bathroom in a resident room, or from one resident's room in another. Dedicated equipment is used in isolation areas or for specific residents where the facility requires it. Do not share equipment between areas unless the procedure allows it, and clean or replace it as directed.

instruction.heading: Containing a cross-contamination event
instruction.body: If a used item reaches a clean area, a clean item reaches a used area, or a glove touches clean stock after touching a soiled surface, treat it as a cross-contamination event. Stop, do not use the affected item or stock, set it aside in a clearly marked place, and tell the supervisor. Do not try to clean it and return it to stock. Record the item, where it was found, what it touched, the time and the person told. The supervisor decides the next step under the facility procedure.

instruction.heading: Worked scenario: the cloth on the clean shelf
instruction.body: You used a cloth in a bathroom and then, without thinking, placed it on the clean trolley shelf to free your hand. You notice it some minutes later. The correct response is to remove it from the clean shelf, put it in the used container or bag, set aside any clean items it has touched, and tell the supervisor. Record the event as a cross-contamination event with the time and the affected items. Do not reuse the cloth or the items that were on the shelf until the supervisor decides.

procedure: Check the facility route and sequence for the area, and confirm the holding area for used items.
Set up the trolley with clean cloths, product and equipment in the clean compartments only.
Work from the least exposed area toward the most exposed, following the facility sequence.
Keep used cloths and items in closed containers, and do not place them on the clean shelf.
If a cross-contamination event occurs, stop, set the affected items aside, and tell the supervisor.
At the end of the round, move used items to the holding area by the designated route, and do not cross back through clean areas.
Record the route used, the segregation applied, any breach and the person told, with the time.

workedExamples.situation: Your route to the far end of a unit passes the soiled linen holding area. The shortest route is through it, and the designated route is longer.
workedExamples.reasoning: Use the designated route, which avoids the soiled holding area. Taking the shortest route would carry contamination past the clean work. If the designated route is blocked, tell the supervisor before you move.

workedExamples.situation: Halfway through a resident room, you realise your bucket has been used in the bathroom and then carried into the room.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do with the bucket and the room?
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop using the bucket for the room. Set it aside in the designated location for used equipment, and get a clean bucket for the zone the facility designates. Tell the supervisor and record the event, including which rooms were affected. The supervisor decides whether any surface needs re-cleaning under the procedure.

equipmentAndPpe: Colour-coded or labelled cloths and equipment for each zone, as provided by the facility
Closed containers or bags for used items, and the designated holding area
Trolley with separate clean and used compartments

commonErrors.error: Carrying a used cloth or equipment into a clean area on the trolley or in a pocket.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep used items in closed containers and in the used compartment only.

commonErrors.error: Taking a shortcut that crosses a soiled area, to save time.
commonErrors.prevention: Follow the designated route. If it is blocked, tell the supervisor before you move.

commonErrors.error: Using a cloth from one zone in another zone.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep each zone's cloths and equipment separate, and follow the facility colour or label system.

commonErrors.error: Returning a cross-contaminated item to stock after cleaning it.
commonErrors.prevention: Set it aside, report the event, and let the supervisor decide the next step.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The NHMRC Australian Guidelines for the Prevention and Control of Infection in Healthcare (2019) treat environmental controls, including cleaning and spill management, as part of preventing transmission from the environment to patients (section 2.2; document dated 2019).

The NDIS Practice Standards, Version 4 of November 2021, Core Module, require that policies cover the storage, handling and disposal of infectious waste, including used PPE, and that workers who handle waste are trained. These requirements apply to the facility where it is an NDIS provider.
Licence notice: Moving used items within a facility does not grant any authority to transport regulated waste off site.

qualityStandard: The learner plans a route on a supplied floor plan that follows the facility sequence and avoids crossing a soiled area.
The learner allocates cloths and equipment to three supplied zones with no cross-zone use.
The learner identifies and contains a cross-contamination event in a supplied scenario, and states the report step.
The learner records the route, segregation and any breach on a completed record.
documentationEvidence: Route and sequence followed, and any deviation with the reason and the supervisor told
Equipment and cloth zones used for each area
Any cross-contamination event, containment action, affected items and person told
summary: Work moves from less contaminated areas to more contaminated areas, and used items do not cross back.
Cloths and equipment are allocated by zone and are not shared across zones without authority.
A cross-contamination event is contained, reported and decided by the supervisor. Do not return items to stock.
Record the route, the segregation and any breach.

knowledgeChecks.question: The shortest route to a room passes a soiled holding area, and the designated route is longer. What should you do?
options: Take the shortest route, since the trolley is covered.
Pass quickly without stopping, so the area is not disturbed.
Use the designated route, and tell the supervisor if it is blocked.

knowledgeChecks.question: A cloth used in a bathroom is placed by mistake on the clean trolley shelf. What is the correct action?
options: Remove it, set aside any clean items it touched, and report the event to the supervisor.
Leave it, since it was only on the shelf briefly and nothing else touched it
Wash the cloth and return it to the clean shelf, since it will then be as good as new

knowledgeChecks.question: How should cloths and equipment be allocated between zones?
options: The same cloths are used in every zone to save time and reduce the number of items to buy
Each zone has its own cloths and equipment, following the facility's colour or label system.
Equipment is shared between zones whenever a zone is busy, so the work keeps moving on the day
